meeting_header: Date: 2025-12-18 | Time: 15:00 PST | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Galaxy Finance), Ethan Brooks (Galaxy), Sofia Li (Galaxy)
summary: Redwood run-through of Eval & Quality Monitoring suite (Console + API + Optimize). Focus on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparison workflows. Customer interested in pilot to validate regression detection and cost/latency tradeoffs in VPC environment. Agreed next steps: security docs, pricing/SOW, pilot start in early Jan.
topics: Private deployment / VPC and security (SOC2, KMS, SSO)
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 40 minutes, we'll do a quick intros and then Diego will walk through the Eval and Quality Monitoring flow in Console and via the API.
00:12 Priya Kapoor: Hi, Priya here, Head of ML at Galaxy Finance. We're looking at a pilot to monitor prompt regressions across our customer-facing flows.
00:20 Maya Chen: Great, thanks Priya. Ethan, Sofia - quick intros?
00:25 Ethan Brooks: Ethan, platform eng, I'll handle VPC and networking details.
00:29 Sofia Li: Sofia, product - mostly focused on product-level alerts and how they'll show up in our dashboards.
00:34 Diego Ramos: Awesome, thanks. Real quick housekeeping: apologies if transcription is a bit off, sometimes the auto captions get deliciously creative, so you'll see small typos. I'll start with the Console demo then show how we wire the API for automated evals.
00:50 Maya Chen: Quick qualification - Priya, you're primarily evaluating for regression detection across prompt changes and model updates?
00:58 Priya Kapoor: Correct. We have a set of canonical prompts for loan approvals and customer queries. We want to detect if a model update or prompt tweak causes drift in intent recognition or hallucinations. Also cost is a concern - token spend across peaks.
01:12 Diego Ramos: Perfect. That maps nicely to three things Redwood Optimize + Console can do: prompt sets management, automated regression alerts (we call them eval alerts), and A/B comparisons between model variants or prompt versions.
01:25 Sofia Li: What's the minimum data we need to feed it? Can we run it on like a hundred prompt variants first?
01:31 Diego Ramos: Yes, you can start with as few as a hundred samples for initial baselines. The Console will compute metrics like ROUGE-ish overlap, semantic similarity with embeddings, and custom classifiers you can plug in. We'll show that.
01:40 Maya Chen: Diego, can you share your screen?
01:44 Diego Ramos: Sure - switching to Console - okay we're on the Eval -> Prompt Sets page. You'll see I have an example "loan_canonical_v1" prompt set. The UI shows per-prompt baselines, metric windows, and an option to attach thresholded alerts.
02:05 Diego Ramos: Here I'm importing a CSV of prompts and expected outputs. Note that the import supports partial matches and also a fuzzy match mode (sometimes transcriptions call it fuzy). That helps with natural language variance.
02:20 Priya Kapoor: The expected outputs - can we store multiple acceptable answers per prompt? We have a few paraphrases.
02:26 Diego Ramos: Yes, you can attach multiple reference responses. The eval engine stores them and computes both strict and soft-match scores. We'll also demo embedding-based similarity thresholds which are less brittle.
02:38 Ethan Brooks: For private deployments - is this data sent to hosted Redwood or stays in our VPC? We're under compliance constraints.
02:45 Diego Ramos: Two options: hosted Redwood where data is retained per your retention policy, or Redwood Private deployed into your VPC or on-prem which keeps all artifacts customer-managed. For the pilot we can do a VPC peering and keep logs in your S3 bucket with encryption.
02:58 Priya Kapoor: KMS?
03:00 Diego Ramos: Yes KMS integration supported; we have notes on HSM for enterprise contracts. I'll share the security pack.
03:06 Maya Chen: That's part of the action items. Diego, can you show regression alerts?
03:10 Diego Ramos: Sure - switching to Alerts tab. Here is a recent alert we generated during a run: model-version bump from rdl-2.1 to rdl-2.2 triggered an increase in semantic drift on the "loan_approval" set. We show the delta with a small sparkline, p95 latency, and token cost estimate.
03:30 Priya Kapoor: How configurable are thresholds? We don't want noisy alerts.
03:34 Diego Ramos: Fully configurable. You can set per-metric thresholds, require N consecutive windows to trigger, and also do composite alerts (e.g., drift above 0.12 and hallucination rate > 2%). And you can route alerts to PagerDuty, Slack, or email.
03:50 Sofia Li: Does the system provide suggested thresholds? Our team is small and not sure where to start.
03:55 Diego Ramos: Optimize offers suggested defaults based on historical variance. It looks at your distribution and suggests a percentile-based threshold; you can accept or tweak.
04:08 Maya Chen: Let's demo an A/B comparison. Diego?
04:11 Diego Ramos: Yep - A/B experiments live here. I'm setting control model rdl-2.1 and candidate rdl-2.2, attaching the same prompt set, and selecting metrics: semantic similarity, answer length, and a custom classifier we call "intent_matcher".
04:30 Diego Ramos: Running a 500-sample A/B run will compute statistical significance and show per-prompt breakdown. Here you can drill into prompts that regressed the most.
04:42 Priya Kapoor: Can we plug in our existing classifier for hallucination detection?
04:46 Diego Ramos: Absolutely. You can upload a model or an API endpoint that returns a label; Redwood will call it as part of the eval pipeline. We log the classifier response alongside the outputs.
04:58 Ethan Brooks: For the API - is there a scheduled eval job endpoint? We want nightly runs against prod traffic samples.
05:05 Diego Ramos: Yes, there's an eval API. You can POST a prompt set reference and options and schedule runs. We also have a streaming ingestion option that does rolling-window evals on live traffic, which then triggers alerts if thresholds are breached.
05:18 Sofia Li: About cost - you mentioned token cost estimates earlier. How precise are they?
05:22 Diego Ramos: They are based on per-token billing estimators and the runtimes you choose; for Dedicated/Private we can use your config to estimate costs. The Console shows estimated spend per-run and cumulative burn.
05:33 Priya Kapoor: Any chance we can do canary rollouts from the A/B results? Like gate a model if regression > X?
05:38 Diego Ramos: Yes - Redwood has rollout policies. You can auto-fallback to previous model when regression breaches a threshold or do gradual ramp-ups. Works across Hosted and Dedicated; for Private there are controls wired to your control plane.
05:52 Maya Chen: There were a few technical questions earlier about KV cache and latency - Diego can you speak to perf tradeoffs during evals?
05:58 Diego Ramos: Sure. When you evaluate long sequences, attention kernels and KV cache behavior matter. For latency-sensitive flows we suggest smaller context windows in eval, and we provide batch simulation to estimate tail latency. The runtime exposes p50/p95/p99 across sequences so you can make tradeoffs.
06:18 Ethan Brooks: If we run the pilot in our VPC, do we still get the same telemetry in Redwood Console?
06:23 Diego Ramos: Yes - telemetry is piped to your Console project; for Private deployments the control plane resides in your VPC and telemetry can be optionally mirrored to Redwood for managed support, or kept internal.
06:35 Priya Kapoor: On the eval metrics - can we create a composite scoring function? Like 0.6*sem_sim + 0.4*(1-hallucination_rate)?
06:43 Diego Ramos: You can. The eval engine supports weighted metrics and custom formulas; they show up in the results and the alerting thresholds can be applied to that composite score.
06:55 Maya Chen: Let's simulate a regression alert quickly. Diego, do a small run and show the UI reaction.
07:00 Diego Ramos: Running a quick 120-sample test... okay results are in. You can see a red flag on "intent_matcher" dropping from 0.94 to 0.81 for candidate. When I click through you can see the failing prompts and the model outputs side-by-side.
07:22 Priya Kapoor: The side-by-side view - can product folks comment inline or annotate?
07:26 Diego Ramos: Yes, you can leave annotations and tag teammates; those comments are persisted on the prompt-level and included in the run history.
07:34 Sofia Li: That's huge for our review flow.
07:36 Maya Chen: Switching gears - security + compliance quick Qs. Priya mentioned SOC2. Diego, what do we have?
07:42 Diego Ramos: We maintain SOC2 Type II reports for Hosted. For Private we provide architecture diagrams and integration docs; we do not manage your keys if you use KMS. We also support SSO/SAML, fine-grained RBAC, and audit logs exported to your SIEM.
07:58 Ethan Brooks: For audit logs - how long are they retained and can we push them to our archive?
08:03 Diego Ramos: Retention configurable per account; typical enterprise setups push logs to customer S3 with lifecycle rules. We'll share the sample config.
08:12 Maya Chen: Okay real quick - timeline and success criteria for the pilot? Priya, what are you looking for?
08:18 Priya Kapoor: We want to validate: 1) regression alerts correctly identify issues with at least 80% precision on our labeled set; 2) A/B results actionable and reproducible; 3) confirm latency/costs in our VPC are within 10% of our target.
08:35 Diego Ramos: Great. For scope I propose a 2-week pilot: one week ingest + baseline, week two A/B and alerts tuning. We'll run a 1k-sample A/B and a nightly rolling eval on production snippets.
08:49 Maya Chen: Sounds good. Any blockers from your side?
08:52 Ethan Brooks: Networking - we'll need Redwood's IP ranges and a minimal IAM role for the peering.
08:58 Diego Ramos: We'll send the IP list and a terraform snippet.
09:02 Priya Kapoor: Also need to confirm data retention and deletion flows for PII.
09:06 Diego Ramos: We'll include the deletion workflow in the security pack.
09:10 Maya Chen: Quick note on costs there may be small egress for hosted but for VPC it's mostly internal - we'll include estimates in the SOW.
09:18 Priya Kapoor: Sounds good.
09:20 Diego Ramos: One more demo item - showing how to baseline and pin a model version in Console so you can gate releases. Here on the Model Management tab you can pin rdl-2.1 for a route and then create a canary route for rdl-2.2 with traffic allocation. If the eval pipeline flags a regression the route can auto-fallback.
09:45 Sofia Li: Do we get a Slack digest or only immediate alerts?
09:49 Diego Ramos: Both - immediate alerts for critical regressions and daily digests summarizing trends and top regressed prompts.
09:56 Priya Kapoor: For A/B reporting - is the significance calculation two-sided t-test or bootstrap?
10:00 Diego Ramos: We use bootstrap by default for non-parametric metrics, and t-tests for mean-shift metrics. You can override the test.
10:12 Maya Chen: Okay, wrapping up. Quick recap and owners?
10:17 Maya Chen: Maya will send pricing and SOW; Diego will send security docs and networking terraform; Priya/Ethan will provide prompt sets and VPC details. Goal: kick pilot around 2026-01-05.
10:28 Priya Kapoor: Confirmed. Appreciate the demo.
10:31 Ethan Brooks: Thanks everyone.
10:33 Diego Ramos: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs.
10:36 Maya Chen: End call.
